decisions.statement: An import, an export and an `import()` each name a module by a specifier.
An import type names a module by the literal in its type argument.
A name handed to `import()` carries a specifier, as one handed to a require does.
A literal handed to `require` or to `require.resolve` names a module.
The first literal a test hands `mock.module` names a module.
A name handed to `mock.module` rather than a literal is not followed.
A literal handed to a name taken from `createRequire`, or to `resolve` on it, names a module.
A name handed there carries a specifier.
A literal a name carrying a specifier is written from names a module.
A parameter handed there makes the argument at that place a specifier at every call.
A function is followed by the name that function is declared or written under.
A `resolve` on anything else names no module.
A specifier built from anything but one plain literal is not seen.
Nothing here reads the disk or the index.

definition: which literals of a body name a module rather than a path
